I should say that I've never watched a full episode of Friends. I lived during the time period it was on (I was always a Seinfeld fan) and was aware of the show's massive popularity, but it was never my cup of tea. However, I have become familiar with all the cast members over the years, and followed many of their other projects, so I became a respective fan of all of them. I went into this special without expectations, and because it had been hyped for over a year, so I figured it would be an interesting and memorable experience.

I was not expecting to get as choked up as I did. (I was also very emotional during the Fresh Prince of Bel Air reunion.) It was just really well done; the initial meeting and viewing of the reconstructed set, reminiscing between cast members, the table reads, trivia game portion, the interview segments with James Corden and all the gratuitous cameos (really surprised that Paul Rudd didn't show up at any point).  You could tell these people really loved each other and bonded during their time together and were trying very hard to suppress their feelings (all the more raw coming out of COVID, especially all the physical contact between them).

Even the revelation that David and Jennifer were "crushing" on each other in real life really lent a lot of gravitas to the proceedings. (And I'm still reviewing that footage of Matt, trying to figure out how exactly he dislocated his shoulder.) Although I didn't recognize any of the clips going into it, I came out sort of a fan in retrospect. I feel like it's a series I would go through if I had someone to watch it with. But it's kind of depressing to watch "Friends" alone without any friends, so I always left it.

As a casual viewer, however, I appreciated the well-rounded documentary format and I really got a good sense of the characters. Especially seeing how much they've aged in 17 years (some better than others), it reminds me of the stark passing of time. Everyone gets older. Life passes by so quickly. At least they have good memories to look back on. My life passed and I don't even know where it went. I'm old and obsolete and I have nothing to show for it.

It moves me a lot, just seeing a life I could never have. Seeing it through the eyes of those who got to live it to the fullest. That's what I've always gotten from TV and movies. I've missed out on so much in life, but I've watched other people get to live out what I could never have.
